long_biography.plain_text:
Industrialist Marcel Bich brought an organiser's methods to France's first sustained America's Cup campaigns. He founded the Association Française pour la Coupe de l'America, financed four challenges between 1970 and 1980 and built design, testing and crew programmes around successive 12-Metre challengers. His opening campaign was the first challenge from outside the English-speaking world.

None reached the Cup match, but Bich's campaigns advanced the idea of multiple challengers and gave French racing design and professional campaign management a durable platform. The America's Cup Hall of Fame later inducted him posthumously, recognising four campaigns and his broader influence on the competition.
